summary: Strong research file. All five financial-model results reproduce exactly (private40 +$14,533 at 0.539 break-even; private20 +$5,363; mixed60 +$3,025; medicaid100 -$19,143; medicaid250 -$24,058), as do every sensitivity figure in the financial narrative and the ~$86/client-month Medicaid contribution. Verified against primary sources: the STAR+PLUS PAS/CFC/respite rates and $3.71/$0.69 split and the $13.00/14% PTB note (HHSC PFD 9/1/2025 sheet); all BLS OEWS 2025 wages (Texas and Houston, four occupations, via O*NET); CareScout 2025 Texas $30/hour, rank 43, 44 h/week; Houston Class B $23.23/sq ft gross (Lee & Associates Q2 2026); the $2,625 initial and three-year renewal fees (§558.3); the 45+45-day time frames (§558.31); the six-month Form 2020 survey request (§558.521); PAS-only administrator and supervisor qualifications (§558.244(a)(3), §558.404(g)); 8+16-hour administrator training (§558.259); renewal 45-day rule (§558.17); the 30-day cure rule; the PHC/CAS rules in Ch. 277 and 40 TAC §48.2918; the franchise tax $2.65M threshold and 50% Medicaid exclusion for HCSSAs; TWC 2.70% on $9,000; IRS 72.5 cents; SOS Form 205 $300; Census QuickFacts; the 198,000 interest-list figure; SPA TX-25-0005; the Aug. 2026 and Sept. 2026 Texas Register proposals; DOL travel-time guidance; the EVV deny/recoup language. Staffing satisfies Chapter 558 (no ratios; qualified administrator, alternate and supervisor). Rent is fixed and sized per configuration. Texas preempts local minimum wages, so no metro adjustment is needed. No critical issues. Main gap: the PHC/CAS/FC rate sheet the file says could not be retrieved is published ($17.13 non-priority / $17.31 priority per hour). Remaining items are citation and wording fixes. HHSC hhs.texas.gov pages (S1, S23, S24, S51, S62) block automated fetches (HTTP 403), so they were checked only through the underlying rules and search snippets. The 512-438-3550 phone number matched the HHSC 'What is PHC?' page in search results.

current.value: Up to 45 days to find the application complete, then up to 45 days to issue (26 TAC §558.31); deficiencies must be answered within 30 days

correct.value: Up to 45 days to find the application complete, then up to 45 days to issue (26 TAC §558.31); missing information must be submitted within 30 days of HHSC's notice or HHSC may deny the application (§558.12)

issues.evidence: The 30-day cure period is in 26 TAC §558.12, not §558.31: 'The applicant must submit to HHSC, through the online portal, the additional information requested to complete the application by no later than 30 days after the date of the notice... If an applicant fails to submit the required information ... within 30 days ... HHSC considers the application incomplete and may deny the application.' §558.31 contains only the two 45-day time frames.
issues.fix: Add a source for 26 TAC §558.12 (url above) and cite it for the 30-day rule in key_numbers[1], checklist[27].cite ('26 TAC §558.12; §558.31') and sections.licensing_pathway Step 4; change 'or the application is denied' to 'or HHSC may deny the application (and keep the fee)'.

issues.correct: HHSC has up to 45 days to find the application complete. If HHSC sends a notice of missing information, submit it within 30 days; otherwise HHSC may deny the application and does not refund the fee.
issues.evidence: 26 TAC §558.12: '...HHSC considers the application incomplete and may deny the application. If HHSC denies the application, HHSC does not refund the license fee.' HHSC sends only one deficiency notice.
